high.title: Ringgit Ends Higher on Robust Economic Data
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar, supported by Malaysia's exceptional trade performance in June 2026, with exports surging 45.4% year-on-year to RM177.9 billion and trade surplus widening 64.9% to RM14.9 billion. The Q2 2026 trade surplus ballooned to RM84 billion from RM63.2 billion in Q1, signaling a stronger current account position. This robust economic data provides strong fundamental support for the ringgit and reflects sustained competitiveness of Malaysian exports.

high.title: Trump Orders New 50% Tariff on Many Canadian Goods
high.summary: Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on a wide range of Canadian goods using the rarely invoked Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, effective in 30 days, and critically these duties will apply even to USMCA-covered products. This escalation in North American trade tensions could ripple into global supply chains and commodity markets, potentially impacting Malaysian exporters who compete with or supply to North American markets. The tariff move also raises broader concerns about global trade stability and inflationary pressures.

high.title: Ringgit retreats on Middle East concerns despite stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 GDP
high.summary: Malaysia's Q2 2026 GDP came in at 5.8%, beating the consensus forecast of 5.3%, signalling strong economic resilience amid global uncertainties. Despite this positive data, the ringgit depreciated to 4.0930/4.0990 against the US dollar, pressured by Middle East concerns. Average H1 2026 GDP growth of 5.6% positions Malaysia on track for approximately 5% full-year growth.

high.title: Bursa higher at close on foreign fund inflows, second quarter GDP
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed 9.26 points higher at 1,731.45, driven by foreign fund inflows and a stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 GDP reading. Softer inflation and a stable overnight policy rate of 2.75% are supporting consumer spending and business investment. Market turnover rose in value to RM3.04 billion, reflecting improved investor sentiment.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on broad-based buying
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 8.43 points at 1,722.19, driven by foreign fund inflows and selective buying in financial, plantation and industrial sectors. Investor confidence is buoyed by expectations that Malaysia's Q2 GDP will exceed 4%, with results due the following day. Wall Street gains from softer US wholesale inflation and strong bank earnings also supported sentiment, raising hopes of Fed rate cuts later in 2026.

high.title: Ringgit rises as soft US data weighs on greenback
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0655/4.0710 against the US dollar after the US PPI unexpectedly fell 0.3% month-on-month in June, weakening the dollar index. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh signalled no urgency to raise interest rates, lending support to emerging market currencies including the ringgit. Lower oil prices following a US-Iran ceasefire also contributed to easing both CPI and PPI pressures.

high.title: Bursa ends lower, weighed by profit-taking in banking, energy stocks
high.summary: The FBM KLCI shed 6.18 points to close at 1,713.76, pressured by profit-taking in banking and energy counters amid geopolitical uncertainty. Despite the weaker headline index, market breadth remained positive with healthcare, consumer and plantation stocks outperforming, signalling a rotation into defensive sectors. Turnover expanded to 4.07 billion units worth RM2.84 billion, reflecting continued active participation.

high.title: Bursa gains on improved sentiment ahead of GDP data
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.15 points to 1,723.09, buoyed by a Wall Street rebound in semiconductor stocks and weaker-than-expected US inflation data for June. The softer inflation figures eased fears of a Fed rate hike, pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.587%, improving risk sentiment across markets. This positive external backdrop, combined with anticipation of Malaysia's Q2 GDP release on Friday, is driving near-term investor interest.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher ahead of Q2 GDP estimate
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0740/4.0780 against the US dollar, ahead of Malaysia's Q2 2026 advance GDP figures due Friday. Economists forecast GDP growth above 5%, supported by strong E&E and commodity exports, though cautious consumer spending may moderate the expansion. The GDP release is a key market-moving event that could significantly influence currency and equity direction.

medium.title: Bursa Closes Lower on Profit-Taking in Banking Stocks
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower due to profit-taking in banking stocks amid mixed regional sentiment, with Brent crude climbing above US$90 per barrel on escalating West Asia tensions raising inflation and interest rate concerns. Analysts highlight sector rotation as a key theme, with energy and plantation counters gaining favour on firmer commodity prices. Sustained foreign fund inflows and selective blue-chip buying are expected to cushion further downside.

medium.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar, Major Currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0920 against the US dollar, buoyed by Malaysia's GDP growth accelerating to 5.8% year-on-year in Q2 2026 from 5.4% in Q1. However, analysts cautioned that geopolitical tensions in West Asia and rising US-Iran hostilities could keep currency markets volatile and support the US Dollar Index. The ringgit's near-term trajectory is seen as dependent on global risk sentiment alongside strong domestic fundamentals.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Higher on Expected Sector Rotation
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened higher at 1,732.59 despite Wall Street declining on semiconductor and AI stock sell-offs and surging crude oil prices amid US-Iran tensions. The local bourse showed resilience with gainers outpacing losers in early trade, reflecting domestic buying interest. Sector rotation into energy and commodity-linked stocks is anticipated as crude oil prices remain elevated.

medium.title: Bursa opens slightly lower on profit-taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened slightly weaker at 1,719.86, weighed down by overnight declines in US semiconductor stocks and profit-taking in the local technology sector. Analysts anticipate downside to be cushioned by optimism surrounding the official launch of the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme. Tactical buying is expected to rotate towards renewable energy and energy storage plays.

medium.title: Ringgit flat against US dollar, higher versus major currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit traded flat against the US dollar ahead of Malaysia's Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate, with analysts projecting a 5.1% growth figure supported by strong E&E export demand. The US Dollar Index edged up 0.28% as some Fed officials maintained a hawkish stance on interest rates. The ringgit was expected to trade within the RM4.06–RM4.08 range pending clarity on US monetary policy.

medium.title: Ringgit firms as US rate hike expectations recede
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0710/4.0745 against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by receding expectations of a US rate hike following softer-than-expected CPI and PPI data. Fed Chair's remarks to the Senate Banking Committee indicated no urgency to raise the federal funds rate, boosting Asian currencies broadly. The ringgit, however, traded mostly lower against a basket of other major currencies.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds on stronger investor appetite
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.30 points to 1,718.06 at the opening bell, supported by improving global risk sentiment following softer US producer inflation data. Malacca Securities noted that technology counters were likely to attract selective buying as expectations for further Fed rate hikes diminished. Early market breadth was mixed with losers slightly outnumbering gainers, indicating cautious but improving sentiment.

medium.title: Ringgit ends flat against US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit closed unchanged at 4.0760/4.0805 against the dollar as positive momentum from lower US CPI was offset by concerns over China's slowing Q2 GDP growth of 4.3%, down from 5% in Q1 2026. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with Trump threatening Iran over Strait of Hormuz incidents, added to cautious trading. The ringgit also weakened against most major currencies at the close.

medium.title: Syahrul Azmir made new CEO of Rapid Bus
medium.summary: Rapid Bus has appointed Syahrul Azmir as its new CEO, bringing over 27 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, and transport sectors from firms including Aramex Malaysia and Kontena Nasional. The appointment signals Rapid Bus's push to improve service reliability and accelerate electric bus deployment across Rapid KL and Rapid Penang networks. This is relevant to investors tracking Malaysia's public transport modernisation and EV transition efforts.
